In the press · Guest post · 11 November 2026

$999,999 Owes Nothing, $1,000,000 Owes $40,000: The Pied-a-Terre Tax Starts at a Cliff

A guest post by Pablo Loschi in Housing Notes, Jonathan Miller's newsletter. The 11 November guest post pre-dates the 15 November correction to the source story, including the clarification that co-ops valued by the city at $1 million or more are covered under the non-primary-residence surcharge. For the current explanation of co-op coverage, valuations, appeals and the 2028 rates, read the source story, updated 15 November, the Second-Home Tax Threshold working paper (v2.0), and the updates log.

Read the guest post →

In the press · Guest post · 12 October 2026

One Dollar Below $2 Million: How a Tax Line Moved NYC's Recorded Prices

Published in Housing Notes, Jonathan Miller's newsletter on the New York housing market and the appraisal industry, which has more than 11,000 subscribers. Miller co-founded the appraisal and consulting firm Miller Samuel in 1986 and for 32 years wrote the Elliman Report, Douglas Elliman's market reports. The post is a short version of the $2 million tax-line story, based on The Shape of the Tax; the October post reports the earlier preprint count at $1,999,999 (131 sales in 2020–2025 vs. 4 before April 2019), whereas the updated story and Tax paper from version 3.0 onward report 127 vs. 4.
